inputs.description: A passive Python network monitor for IoT devices such as thermostats, IP cameras, smart lights and badge readers, which cannot run security software. It learns a behavioural baseline per device type, detects new destinations, C2 beaconing, volume spikes, scanning and rogue devices, scores each device 0 to 100, tags findings with MITRE ATT&CK, raises de-duplicated alerts, shows an offline dashboard and generates quarantine scripts. Constraints: one person, simulated traffic, free tools, fixed deadline.

content.objective: Build a passive network monitor that learns normal behaviour per IoT device type and detects compromised devices, scoring their risk and recommending containment.
content.success_criteria: Detect every injected attack with 0 false alarms on clean traffic; every alert explained and ATT&CK-tagged; all automated tests passing.
content.key_deliverables:
Python monitoring system (capture, flows, inventory, baseline, detectors)
Risk scoring, alerting and quarantine scripts
Offline SOC-style dashboard
Evaluation, evasion and fleet results
Synopsis, project report and presentation
high_level_requirements: Passively read traffic from a pcap file or mirror port
Identify every device, including unregistered ones
Learn a baseline per device type from one clean day
Detect new destinations, beaconing, volume spikes, rhythm changes and scans
Score risk 0-100 and map findings to MITRE ATT&CK
Alert without duplicates and generate quarantine scripts for score 100

milestones.milestone: Report v1 delivered (original plan end: Day 24)

risks: No real labelled IoT data or hardware
Alert fatigue from many alerts per incident
